This diminutive starting point, characteristic of anostracan crustaceans, marks the beginning of a rapid growth trajectory that unfolds in ephemeral freshwater pools across their European range. Field surveys indicate that newly hatched nauplii begin filter feeding almost immediately, grazing upon phytoplankton and bacterial aggregates suspended in the water column. The initial body size imposes constraints on early foraging efficiency, as the small filtering apparatus can only process a narrow range of particle sizes. Nevertheless, the larval stages progress swiftly through a series of ecdyses, with each moult facilitating a measurable increase in body dimensions. Comparative data from related chirocephalid species suggest that the duration of the naupliar phase is strongly temperature-dependent, with warmer conditions accelerating developmental rates. For Chirocephalus carnuntanus, the period between hatching and the onset of juvenile morphology is typically brief, a strategy that minimizes exposure to predation and desiccation risk in their temporary aquatic habitats.
